note.question: How does the finite-mixture logit model affect price optimization?
note.overview: The model considers price optimization under the finite-mixture logit model. This model assumes that customers belong to one of a number of customer segments, where each customer segment chooses according to a multinomial logit model with segment-specific parameters. We reformulate the corresponding price optimization problem and develop a novel characterization.

In a numerical simulation with randomly drawn parameter values, price optimization under the incorrect assumption of a multinomial logit demand model (that ignores customer segmentation) led to a revenue loss of more than 20% in more than 30% of the tested instances.

conditions: In this section, we present our branch-and-bound algorithm that computes a (1 −ε)-approximation for the revenue maximization problem when customers choose according to the FML choice model.
For any ε > 0, BNB(ε) generates a vector of no-purchase probabilities x′ ∈X such that π(x′) ≥(1 −ε)maxx∈Xπ(x).
By Proposition 2, this vector x′ corresponds with a price vector p′ ∈Rn that is ε-optimal: (1 −ε)Π(p′) ≥maxp∈RnΠ(p).
